title: Join the third control-plane node
instructions: Two of the three control-plane nodes are already joined. The third has been prepared but never joined. Generate a fresh bootstrap token and a certificate key, join the third control-plane node with kubeadm, and confirm the API endpoint serves three etcd members.
steps: On the first control-plane node run `kubectl get nodes` and note there are two control-plane nodes and two workers.
Generate a certificate key with `sudo kubeadm init phase upload-certs --upload-certs` and note the 64-character key.
Create a join command with `sudo kubeadm token create --print-join-command`.

Find the unjoined controller's IP: it is the address in `~/.ssh/painkiller_known_hosts` that is not yet listed as a node. SSH there and run the join command, appending `--control-plane --certificate-key <key>`.
Verify with `kubectl get nodes` (three control-plane Ready) and `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l component=etcd` (three Running members).
solution:
joined=$(kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '[.items[].status.addresses[] | select(.type=="InternalIP") | .address] | unique | .[]')
all=$(awk '!/^#/ {print $1}' "$HOME/.ssh/painkiller_known_hosts")
third=$(comm -23 <(printf '%s\n' "$all" | sort -u) <(printf '%s\n' "$joined" | sort -u) | head -1)
key=$(sudo -n kubeadm init phase upload-certs --upload-certs 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
join=$(sudo -n kubeadm token create --print-join-command)
ssh "$third" "sudo -n $join --control-plane --certificate-key $key"
resource: jq -n --argjson nodes "$(kubectl get nodes -o json)" --argjson etcd "$(kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd -o json)" '{nodes:$nodes,etcd:$etcd}'

checks.description: All three control-plane nodes are Ready
checks.expression: ([.nodes.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] != null)] | length) == 3 and ([.nodes.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] != null and ([.status.conditions[]? | select(.type=="Ready")][0].status == "True"))] | length) == 3

explanation: A stacked-etcd HA cluster joins additional control-plane nodes with `kubeadm join --control-plane --certificate-key`. The certificate key is uploaded on demand and expires after two hours, so it must be generated as part of the join rather than assumed from preparation.

title: Drain a worker safely and back up etcd
instructions: Cordon and drain one worker node while respecting the `web-pdb` PodDisruptionBudget in `exam-workloads`, saving the drain output to `/tmp/drain-evidence.txt`, then return (uncordon) the worker. Finally create an etcd snapshot at `/opt/backup/etcd.db` on the control-plane node and confirm it is readable.
steps: Pick a worker with `kubectl get nodes` and cordon it with `kubectl cordon <worker>`.
Drain it with `kubectl drain <worker> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data` so its Pods reschedule without violating the PDB, and record the output with `2>&1 | tee /tmp/drain-evidence.txt`.
Confirm `kubectl get pods -n exam-workloads` still shows the `web` Pods running, then uncordon with `kubectl uncordon <worker>`.
On a control-plane node run `sudo -n mkdir -p /opt/backup` and `sudo -n env ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /opt/backup/etcd.db`.
Validate with `sudo -n env ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /opt/backup/etcd.db -w json` and confirm `totalKey` is greater than zero.
solution:
worker=$(kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] == null)][0].metadata.name')
kubectl cordon "$worker"
kubectl drain "$worker" --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --timeout=180s 2>&1 | tee /tmp/drain-evidence.txt
kubectl uncordon "$worker"
sudo -n mkdir -p /opt/backup
sudo -n env ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/server.key snapshot save /opt/backup/etcd.db
resource: jq -n --argjson snap "$(sudo -n env ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot status /opt/backup/etcd.db -w json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson evidence "$(test -s /tmp/drain-evidence.txt && grep -Eq 'cordoned|evicting|drained|evicted' /tmp/drain-evidence.txt && echo true || echo false)" '{snapshot:$snap,evidence:$evidence}'

checks.description: The etcd snapshot is readable and populated

explanation: `kubectl drain` evicts Pods after a cordon, and `--delete-emptydir-data` and `--ignore-daemonsets` are needed for many workloads. Because a completed drain is a historical action, the saved output is the evidence of a successful, PDB-respecting drain. `etcdctl snapshot save` captures a consistent etcd backup that `snapshot status` can read back.

title: Grant least-privilege Pod log access
instructions: In namespace `exam-rbac`, create a Role named `pod-log-reader` that allows `get` and `list` on `pods` and `pods/log`, and bind it to the ServiceAccount `auditor` with a RoleBinding named `read-pod-logs`. The auditor must be able to read Pod logs but must be denied Secrets and access to other namespaces.
steps: Create the Role with `kubectl -n exam-rbac create role pod-log-reader --verb=get,list --resource=pods,pods/log`.
Bind it with `kubectl -n exam-rbac create rolebinding read-pod-logs --role=pod-log-reader --serviceaccount=exam-rbac:auditor`.
Verify with `kubectl auth can-i get pods/logs -n exam-rbac --as=system:serviceaccount:exam-rbac:auditor` (should print yes).
Verify denial with `kubectl auth can-i get secrets -n exam-rbac --as=system:serviceaccount:exam-rbac:auditor` and a cross-namespace `list pods -n kube-system` check (both should print no).
solution:
kubectl -n exam-rbac create role pod-log-reader --verb=get,list --resource=pods,pods/log
kubectl -n exam-rbac create rolebinding read-pod-logs --role=pod-log-reader --serviceaccount=exam-rbac:auditor
resource: jq -n --argjson role "$(kubectl -n exam-rbac get role pod-log-reader -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson rb "$(kubectl -n exam-rbac get rolebinding read-pod-logs -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson canlogs "$(kubectl auth can-i get pods/logs -n exam-rbac --as=system:serviceaccount:exam-rbac:auditor 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^yes$' && echo true || echo false)" --argjson cansecret "$(kubectl auth can-i get secrets -n exam-rbac --as=system:serviceaccount:exam-rbac:auditor 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^yes$' && echo true || echo false)" --argjson cancross "$(kubectl auth can-i list pods -n kube-system --as=system:serviceaccount:exam-rbac:auditor 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^yes$' && echo true || echo false)" '{role:$role,rolebinding:$rb,can_logs:$canlogs,can_secrets:$cansecret,can_cross_ns:$cancross}'

checks.description: Role grants Pod and Pod-log read access
checks.expression: (.role != null) and any(.role.rules[]?; (.apiGroups | index("") != null) and (.resources | index("pods") != null) and (.resources | index("pods/log") != null) and (.verbs | index("get") != null) and (.verbs | index("list") != null))

checks.description: RoleBinding binds the Role to the auditor
checks.expression: (.rolebinding != null) and .rolebinding.roleRef.kind == "Role" and .rolebinding.roleRef.name == "pod-log-reader" and any(.rolebinding.subjects[]?; .kind == "ServiceAccount" and .name == "auditor" and .namespace == "exam-rbac")

checks.description: Auditor is denied Secrets and cross-namespace access

explanation: A Role grants permissions within one namespace, and a RoleBinding attaches it to a ServiceAccount. `pods/log` is a distinct subresource, and denying Secrets plus cross-namespace access demonstrates least privilege.

title: Repair a Helm release and deploy a Kustomize overlay
instructions: A Helm release named `demo` in `exam-helm` was installed with an unpullable image tag. Repair it with `helm upgrade` so it runs `nginx:1.27` while staying Helm-managed. Then deploy the supplied Kustomize overlay at `/opt/painkiller/cka002/kustomize/overlay` to create `kustom-app` with three replicas, without editing the base.
steps: Inspect the release with `helm -n exam-helm list` and `kubectl -n exam-helm get deploy demo-web`.
Repair it with `helm upgrade demo /opt/painkiller/cka002/chart -n exam-helm --set image.tag=1.27`.
Confirm with `kubectl -n exam-helm get deploy demo-web` (one available replica, image `nginx:1.27`).
Review the base and overlay under `/opt/painkiller/cka002/kustomize/`, then apply with `kubectl apply -k /opt/painkiller/cka002/kustomize/overlay`.
Verify `kubectl -n exam-helm get deploy kustom-app` shows three replicas.
solution:
helm upgrade demo /opt/painkiller/cka002/chart -n exam-helm --set image.tag=1.27
kubectl -n exam-helm rollout status deployment/demo-web --timeout=180s
kubectl apply -k /opt/painkiller/cka002/kustomize/overlay
kubectl -n exam-helm rollout status deployment/kustom-app --timeout=180s
resource: jq -n --argjson helm "$(kubectl -n exam-helm get deployment demo-web -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson kustom "$(kubectl -n exam-helm get deployment kustom-app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{helm:$helm,kustom:$kustom}'

checks.description: Helm release uses the correct image and stays Helm-managed
Helm release has one available replica

explanation: `helm upgrade` reconciles a release with new values while preserving its Helm ownership labels. Kustomize overlays layer patches on a shared base, so the base stays untouched while the overlay changes replica count and namespace.

title: Install a CRD and operator
instructions: Install the supplied `Widget` CRD and its operator from `/opt/painkiller/cka002/operator/`, create a `Widget` custom resource in `exam-ops`, and verify the operator reconciles it into a ConfigMap.
steps: Apply the CRD and operator with `kubectl apply -f /opt/painkiller/cka002/operator/`.
Wait for the operator with `kubectl -n exam-ops rollout status deployment/widget-operator`.

Create a Widget named `demo` with `kubectl -n exam-ops apply -f - <<< 'apiVersion: example.painkiller.io/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: demo
spec:
  message: hello'`.
Wait a few seconds and verify `kubectl -n exam-ops get configmap demo-reconciled` exists and carries `message: hello`.
solution:
kubectl apply -f /opt/painkiller/cka002/operator/
kubectl -n exam-ops rollout status deployment/widget-operator --timeout=180s
kubectl -n exam-ops apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: example.painkiller.io/v1
kind: Widget
metadata:
  name: demo
spec:
  message: hello
YAML
resource: jq -n --argjson crd "$(kubectl get crd widgets.example.painkiller.io -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson operator "$(kubectl -n exam-ops get deployment widget-operator -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson widgets "$(kubectl -n exam-ops get widgets.example.painkiller.io -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson cm "$(kubectl -n exam-ops get configmap -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{crd:$crd,operator:$operator,widgets:$widgets,configmaps:$cm}'
explanation: A CustomResourceDefinition extends the API, and an operator is a controller that watches those resources and reconciles the desired state into other objects. Here the operator materializes each Widget into a ConfigMap.

title: Recover a rollout with probes and rolling-update limits
instructions: The Deployment `app` in `exam-workloads` cannot start because its image is invalid. Fix it to `nginx:1.27`, add a readiness and a liveness probe, and constrain rolling updates so no more than one Pod is replaced at a time (maxUnavailable 0).
steps: Inspect with `kubectl -n exam-workloads describe deployment app` to see the image pull failure.
Fix the image with `kubectl -n exam-workloads set image deployment/app app=nginx:1.27`.
Edit the Deployment with `kubectl -n exam-workloads edit deployment app` and add `readinessProbe` and `livenessProbe` (httpGet on port 80).
Set `spec.strategy.type: RollingUpdate` with `rollingUpdate.maxUnavailable: 0` and `maxSurge: 1`.
Wait with `kubectl -n exam-workloads rollout status deployment/app` and confirm two available replicas.
solution:
kubectl -n exam-workloads set image deployment/app app=nginx:1.27
kubectl -n exam-workloads rollout status deployment/app --timeout=180s
kubectl -n exam-workloads patch deployment app --type=strategic -p '{"spec":{"strategy":{"type":"RollingUpdate","rollingUpdate":{"maxUnavailable":0,"maxSurge":1}},"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"app","readinessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80}},"livenessProbe":{"httpGet":{"path":"/","port":80}}}]}}}}'
kubectl -n exam-workloads rollout status deployment/app --timeout=180s
resource: kubectl -n exam-workloads get deployment app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null

checks.description: Deployment runs the required image and is available
Rolling update never drops below the replica count

explanation: An invalid image leaves a Deployment without available replicas. Readiness probes gate traffic, liveness probes restart stuck containers, and `maxUnavailable: 0` ensures the old replicas stay up until replacements are ready.

title: Configure an application with a CPU autoscaler
instructions: In `exam-workloads`, configure the Deployment `hpa-web` to mount the ConfigMap `app-config` at `/etc/config` and the Secret `app-secret` at `/etc/secret`. Give its container a CPU request of `100m`, then create a HorizontalPodAutoscaler named `hpa-web` that scales it between 1 and 5 replicas at 50% CPU.
steps: Edit the Deployment with `kubectl -n exam-workloads edit deployment hpa-web` and add the two volumes and volume mounts.
Add `resources.requests.cpu: 100m` to the container.
Wait with `kubectl -n exam-workloads rollout status deployment/hpa-web`.
Create the HPA with `kubectl -n exam-workloads autoscale deployment hpa-web --min=1 --max=5 --cpu=50%`.
Verify with `kubectl -n exam-workloads get hpa hpa-web` (metrics require the metrics server, which is installed).
solution:
kubectl -n exam-workloads patch deployment hpa-web --type=strategic -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"web","resources":{"requests":{"cpu":"100m"}},"volumeMounts":[{"name":"config","mountPath":"/etc/config"},{"name":"secret","mountPath":"/etc/secret"}]}],"volumes":[{"name":"config","configMap":{"name":"app-config"}},{"name":"secret","secret":{"secretName":"app-secret"}}]}}}}'
kubectl -n exam-workloads rollout status deployment/hpa-web --timeout=180s
kubectl -n exam-workloads autoscale deployment hpa-web --min=1 --max=5 --cpu=50%
resource: jq -n --argjson dep "$(kubectl -n exam-workloads get deployment hpa-web -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson hpa "$(kubectl -n exam-workloads get hpa hpa-web -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{deployment:$dep,hpa:$hpa}'

checks.expression: (.hpa != null) and .hpa.spec.scaleTargetRef.name == "hpa-web" and .hpa.spec.minReplicas == 1 and .hpa.spec.maxReplicas == 5 and any(.hpa.spec.metrics[]?; .type == "Resource" and .resource.name == "cpu" and .resource.target.averageUtilization == 50)

explanation: ConfigMaps and Secrets configure applications as mounted files or environment variables. A CPU HPA needs a CPU request as its baseline and the metrics server to read actual utilization.

title: Pin scheduling with affinity, toleration, and spread
instructions: One worker carries the taint `exam=reserved:NoSchedule`. Create a Deployment named `pinned` in `exam-workloads` (3 replicas, image `nginx:1.27`) that tolerates that taint, requires the `topology.kubernetes.io/zone` node affinity, spreads across zones with `maxSkew: 1`, and runs three available replicas. Also create a ResourceQuota named `exam-quota` in `exam-workloads` limiting Pods to 10.
steps: Inspect the taint with `kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '[.items[].spec.taints]'`.
Create the Deployment with a toleration for `exam=reserved:NoSchedule`, required node affinity on `topology.kubernetes.io/zone`, and a topologySpreadConstraint on the same key with `maxSkew: 1`.
Wait with `kubectl -n exam-workloads rollout status deployment/pinned` and confirm three replicas.
Create the quota with `kubectl -n exam-workloads create quota exam-quota --hard=pods=10`.
solution:
kubectl -n exam-workloads create quota exam-quota --hard=pods=10
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: pinned
  namespace: exam-workloads
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: pinned
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: pinned
    spec:
      tolerations:
        - key: exam
          value: reserved
          effect: NoSchedule
      affinity:
        nodeAffinity:
          requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
            nodeSelectorTerms:
              - matchExpressions:
                  - key: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
                    operator: In
                    values: [west, east]
      topologySpreadConstraints:
        - maxSkew: 1
          topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone
          whenUnsatisfiable: DoNotSchedule
          labelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: pinned
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: nginx:1.27
YAML
kubectl -n exam-workloads rollout status deployment/pinned --timeout=180s
resource: jq -n --argjson dep "$(kubectl -n exam-workloads get deployment pinned -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson quota "$(kubectl -n exam-workloads get resourcequota -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{deployment:$dep,quota:$quota}'

checks.description: Required node affinity targets a zone

explanation: Tolerations let Pods land on tainted nodes, required node affinity constrains where they run, and topology spread distributes replicas across a topology key. A ResourceQuota bounds how much a namespace may consume.

title: Isolate a database with NetworkPolicy
instructions: In `exam-netpol`, create a NetworkPolicy named `allow-web` that selects the Pod `db` and allows ingress only from Pods labeled `app=web` on port 80. After applying it, the `web` Pod must still reach `db` and resolve it via DNS, while the `other` Pod must be denied.
steps: Inspect the Pods with `kubectl -n exam-netpol get pods --show-labels`.
Create the NetworkPolicy selecting `app=db` with ingress from `app=web` on port 80.
Apply it and verify enforcement with `kubectl -n exam-netpol exec web -- wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null http://db` (should succeed).
Verify denial with `kubectl -n exam-netpol exec other -- wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null http://db` (should fail).
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-web
  namespace: exam-netpol
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: web
      ports:
        - port: 80
YAML
resource: jq -n --argjson np "$(kubectl -n exam-netpol get networkpolicy allow-web -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson webdb "$(kubectl -n exam-netpol exec web -- sh -c 'wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null http://db 2>/dev/null && echo true || echo false' 2>/dev/null || echo false)" --argjson otherdb "$(kubectl -n exam-netpol exec other -- sh -c 'wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null http://db 2>/dev/null && echo true || echo false' 2>/dev/null || echo false)" --argjson dns "$(kubectl -n exam-netpol exec web -- sh -c 'nslookup db 2>/dev/null | grep -qi address && echo true || echo false' 2>/dev/null || echo false)" '{np:$np,web_db:$webdb,other_db:$otherdb,dns:$dns}'

checks.description: NetworkPolicy allows only the web client
checks.expression: (.np != null) and .np.spec.podSelector.matchLabels.app == "db" and any(.np.spec.ingress[]?; any(.from[]?; (.podSelector.matchLabels.app == "web")) and any(.ports[]?; .port == 80))

checks.description: The authorized client still reaches db
Cluster DNS still resolves the service

explanation: Calico enforces NetworkPolicy. The policy denies by default for the selected Pod and re-allows only the labeled client, while DNS (egress) remains open so service names keep resolving.

title: Route across namespaces with the Gateway API
instructions: Using the installed Envoy Gateway, create a Gateway on port 80, an HTTPRoute that routes host `gw.example.com` path `/` to the Service `backend` in namespace `exam-gw-backend` (a cross-namespace backend), and a ReferenceGrant in `exam-gw-backend` that authorizes the route's namespace.
steps: Create a Gateway in `exam-gw` with a listener on port 80 using the `eg` GatewayClass.
Create a ReferenceGrant in `exam-gw-backend` permitting HTTPRoute from the `exam-gw` namespace to the `backend` Service.
Create an HTTPRoute in `exam-gw` with hostname `gw.example.com` and a backendRef to `backend` in `exam-gw-backend`.
Wait for the Envoy proxy and confirm `kubectl -n exam-gw get httproute` shows Accepted and ResolvedRefs conditions as True.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: GatewayClass
metadata:
  name: eg
spec:
  controllerName: gateway.envoyproxy.io/gatewayclass-controller
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: exam
  namespace: exam-gw
spec:
  gatewayClassName: eg
  listeners:
    - name: http
      protocol: HTTP
      port: 80
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: ReferenceGrant
metadata:
  name: allow-exam-gw
  namespace: exam-gw-backend
spec:
  from:
    - group: gateway.networking.k8s.io
      kind: HTTPRoute
      namespace: exam-gw
  to:
    - group: ""
      kind: Service
      name: backend
---
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: HTTPRoute
metadata:
  name: exam
  namespace: exam-gw
spec:
  parentRefs:
    - name: exam
      namespace: exam-gw
  hostnames:
    - gw.example.com
  rules:
    - matches:
        - path:
            type: PathPrefix
            value: /
      backendRefs:
        - name: backend
          namespace: exam-gw-backend
          port: 80
YAML
resource: jq -n --argjson gw "$(kubectl get gateway -A -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson route "$(kubectl get httproute -A -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson grant "$(kubectl get referencegrant -A -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{gateways:$gw,httproutes:$route,referencegrants:$grant}'

checks.description: HTTPRoute routes to a cross-namespace backend
checks.expression: (.httproutes != null) and any(.httproutes.items[]?; any(.spec.rules[]?; any(.matches[]?; .path.value == "/") and any(.backendRefs[]?; .name != null and .namespace != null and .namespace != "")))
(.httproutes != null) and any(.httproutes.items[]?; any(.status.parents[]?; all(.conditions[]?; .status == "True" and (.reason == "Accepted" or .reason == "ResolvedRefs"))))

explanation: The Gateway API separates routing (HTTPRoute) from infrastructure (Gateway). A cross-namespace backendRef must be authorized by a ReferenceGrant in the backend's namespace, or the route fails resolution.

title: Expose an application with Ingress and NodePort
instructions: In `exam-ingress`, create an Ingress named `web` that routes host `ing.example.com` to the Service `web` on port 80 using the `traefik` IngressClass. Also create a NodePort Service named `web-np` (port 80 to targetPort 80) selecting the `web` Deployment, and confirm it has ready endpoints.
steps: Create the Ingress with ingressClassName `traefik`, host `ing.example.com`, and a backend to Service `web` port 80.
Create the NodePort Service `web-np` selecting `app: web` on port 80.
Verify with `kubectl -n exam-ingress get ingress web` and `kubectl -n exam-ingress get svc web-np`.
Confirm endpoints with `kubectl -n exam-ingress get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web-np`.
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata:
  name: web
  namespace: exam-ingress
spec:
  ingressClassName: traefik
  rules:
    - host: ing.example.com
      http:
        paths:
          - path: /
            pathType: Prefix
            backend:
              service:
                name: web
                port:
                  number: 80
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: web-np
  namespace: exam-ingress
spec:
  type: NodePort
  selector:
    app: web
  ports:
    - port: 80
      targetPort: 80
YAML
resource: jq -n --argjson ingress "$(kubectl -n exam-ingress get ingress web -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson svc "$(kubectl -n exam-ingress get svc web-np -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson eps "$(kubectl -n exam-ingress get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=web-np -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{ingress:$ingress,service:$svc,endpoints:$eps}'

checks.description: Ingress routes the host to the backend service
checks.expression: (.ingress != null) and any(.ingress.spec.rules[]?; .host == "ing.example.com" and any(.http.paths[]?; .backend.service.name == "web" and .backend.service.port.number == 80)) and .ingress.spec.ingressClassName == "traefik"
(.service != null) and .service.spec.type == "NodePort" and .service.spec.selector.app == "web" and any(.service.spec.ports[]?; .port == 80 and .targetPort == 80 and .nodePort > 0)
(.endpoints != null) and any(.endpoints.items[]?; any(.endpoints[]?; (.conditions.ready != false) and (.addresses | length) > 0))

explanation: An Ingress is an API rule consumed by an Ingress controller (here Traefik). A NodePort Service allocates a port on every node and forwards to the selected Pods, whose readiness is reflected in endpoint slices.

title: Repair a LoadBalancer allocation
instructions: The Service `lb-app` in `exam-lb` requests a reserved address outside the MetalLB pool, so it never receives an external IP. Remove the invalid request so MetalLB allocates an address from `192.168.254.81–89`, and confirm the service is reachable on that address.
steps: Inspect with `kubectl -n exam-lb describe service lb-app` and note the external IP is stuck pending.
Remove the `metallb.universe.tf/loadBalancerIPs` annotation from the Service.
Wait a moment and confirm `kubectl -n exam-lb get svc lb-app` shows an external IP in the reserved pool.
Probe it with `wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null http://<external-ip>`.
solution:
kubectl -n exam-lb annotate service lb-app metallb.universe.tf/loadBalancerIPs-
kubectl -n exam-lb wait --for=jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress}' service/lb-app --timeout=120s
resource: jq -n --argjson lb "$(kubectl -n exam-lb get svc lb-app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson reach "$(ip=$(kubectl -n exam-lb get svc lb-app -o jsonpath='{.status.loadBalancer.ingress[0].ip}' 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$ip" ] && wget -q -T 3 -O /dev/null http://$ip 2>/dev/null && echo true || echo false)" '{lb:$lb,reachable:$reach}'

checks.description: The invalid allocation request was removed
The service is reachable on its address

explanation: MetalLB assigns LoadBalancer IPs from an IPAddressPool. A Service annotation requesting an address outside the pool keeps the service pending until the request is removed and the speaker advertises the allocated address.

title: Provision dynamic storage with delayed binding
instructions: In `exam-storage`, create a StorageClass named `exam-sc` (provisioner `rancher.io/local-path`, `WaitForFirstConsumer`, `Retain`), a PVC named `exam-pvc` requesting 1Gi from it, and a Pod named `data-app` that mounts the claim at `/data`. The claim must bind and the bound volume must use `Retain`.
steps: Create the StorageClass with `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer` and `reclaimPolicy: Retain`.
Create the PVC `exam-pvc` (1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, storageClassName `exam-sc`).
Create the Pod `data-app` (nginx) mounting the PVC at `/data`; the claim binds only once the Pod is scheduled.
Verify with `kubectl -n exam-storage get pvc exam-pvc` (Bound) and `kubectl get pv` (a dynamically created PV with Retain).
solution:
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: exam-sc
provisioner: rancher.io/local-path
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
reclaimPolicy: Retain
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: exam-pvc
  namespace: exam-storage
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: exam-sc
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: data-app
  namespace: exam-storage
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.27
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /data
  volumes:
    - name: data
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: exam-pvc
YAML
resource: jq -n --argjson sc "$(kubectl get storageclass exam-sc -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson pvc "$(kubectl -n exam-storage get pvc exam-pvc -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson pod "$(kubectl -n exam-storage get pod data-app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson pv "$(kubectl get pv -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{storageclass:$sc,pvc:$pvc,pod:$pod,pvs:$pv}'

checks.description: StorageClass uses delayed binding and Retain
Bound volume retains data on release

explanation: A StorageClass drives dynamic provisioning. `WaitForFirstConsumer` delays binding until a Pod is scheduled (so the volume lands on the right node), and `Retain` preserves the underlying data after the claim is released.

title: Recover a static local volume binding
instructions: A static local PV `exam-local-pv` and a PVC `exam-local-pvc` in `exam-storage` fail to bind: the PVC requests the wrong StorageClass and the PV's node affinity names a non-existent worker. Fix both so the claim binds, then run a Pod named `local-app` that mounts the claim at `/mnt` and can read the supplied file `data.txt`.
steps: Inspect with `kubectl -n exam-storage get pvc exam-local-pvc` (Pending) and `kubectl get pv exam-local-pv -o yaml`.
Change the PVC's `storageClassName` to `exam-local`.
Fix the PV's node affinity so `kubernetes.io/hostname` names a real worker (`kubectl get nodes` lists them).
Create the Pod `local-app` mounting the PVC at `/mnt`.
Verify `kubectl -n exam-storage exec local-app -- cat /mnt/data.txt` prints `painkiller-data`.
solution:
worker=$(kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] == null)][0].metadata.name')
kubectl -n exam-storage delete pvc exam-local-pvc --ignore-not-found
kubectl -n exam-storage apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: exam-local-pvc
  namespace: exam-storage
spec:
  accessModes: [ReadWriteOnce]
  storageClassName: exam-local
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 1Gi
YAML
kubectl patch pv exam-local-pv --type=json -p "[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/nodeAffinity/required/nodeSelectorTerms/0/matchExpressions/0/values/0","value":"$worker"}]"
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: local-app
  namespace: exam-storage
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
      volumeMounts:
        - name: data
          mountPath: /mnt
  volumes:
    - name: data
      persistentVolumeClaim:
        claimName: exam-local-pvc
YAML
resource: jq -n --argjson nodes "$(kubectl get nodes -o json)" --argjson pvc "$(kubectl -n exam-storage get pvc exam-local-pvc -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson pv "$(kubectl get pv exam-local-pv -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson pod "$(kubectl -n exam-storage get pod local-app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --arg data "$(kubectl -n exam-storage exec local-app -- cat /mnt/data.txt 2>/dev/null || echo '')" '{nodes:$nodes,pvc:$pvc,pv:$pv,pod:$pod,data:$data}'

checks.description: Claim binds to the local volume
Local volume targets a real worker
checks.expression: . as $root | (.pv != null) and .pv.spec.local.path == "/opt/painkiller/local-data" and .pv.spec.capacity.storage == "1Gi" and any(.pv.spec.nodeAffinity.required.nodeSelectorTerms[].matchExpressions[]?; .key == "kubernetes.io/hostname" and any(.values[]?; . as $v | any($root.nodes.items[]?; select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] == null) | .metadata.name == $v)))

checks.description: Application Pod runs on the volume

explanation: A static local PV binds by storage class, capacity, and access mode, and its mandatory node affinity pins it to a node. Fixing both the claim's class and the volume's node affinity lets the Pod schedule and read the preserved data.

title: Repair a worker kubelet
instructions: One worker's kubelet configuration has been corrupted, so the node is NotReady. Repair `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml` on the affected worker and restart kubelet so the node becomes Ready again without losing its identity or workloads.
steps: Find the NotReady worker with `kubectl get nodes` and note its IP with `kubectl get nodes -o wide`.
SSH to the worker and inspect `sudo systemctl status kubelet` and `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`.
Remove the corrupted line and run `sudo systemctl restart kubelet`.
Verify `kubectl get nodes` shows all workers Ready.
solution:
worker=$(kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] == null and ([.status.conditions[]? | select(.type=="Ready")][0].status != "True"))][0].metadata.name')
ip=$(kubectl get node "$worker" -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}')
ssh "$ip" 'sudo sed -i "/painkiller-fault/d" /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml && sudo systemctl restart kubelet'
resource: jq -n --argjson nodes "$(kubectl get nodes -o json)" --argjson kubelet "$(w=$(kubectl get nodes -o json | jq -r '[.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] == null)][0].metadata.name'); ip=$(kubectl get node "$w" -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}'); ssh -o ConnectTimeout=5 "$ip" 'sudo systemctl is-active kubelet' 2>/dev/null | grep -qx active && echo true || echo false)" '{nodes:$nodes,kubelet:$kubelet}'

checks.expression: ([.nodes.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] == null)] | length) >= 2 and all(.nodes.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"] == null); ([.status.conditions[]? | select(.type=="Ready")][0].status // "False") == "True")

checks.description: Kubelet is active on the worker

explanation: The kubelet reads `/var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml`; a malformed entry stops it and the node goes NotReady. Removing the bad line and restarting kubelet restores readiness while the node name and running workloads are preserved.

title: Repair a broken scheduler static Pod
instructions: One control-plane node's kube-scheduler static Pod manifest uses an invalid image, so its scheduler cannot start. Identify the node, repair `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml` there, and confirm every scheduler is running again without resetting the cluster.
steps: Find the failing scheduler with `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o wide`.
SSH to the affected control-plane node and edit `/etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml`.
Replace the invalid image with the correct `registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler` tag matching the cluster version.
The kubelet restarts the static Pod automatically; confirm all scheduler Pods are Running.
solution:
bad=$(kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.containers[]?; (.image | contains("9.9.9")))) | .spec.nodeName')
ip=$(kubectl get node "$bad" -o jsonpath='{.status.addresses[?(@.type=="InternalIP")].address}')
ver=$(kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}')
ssh "$ip" "sudo sed -i "s#kube-scheduler:.*#kube-scheduler:${ver}#" /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-scheduler.yaml"
resource: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-scheduler -o json

checks.description: No scheduler uses a broken image

explanation: Static Pods are declared by manifests in `/etc/kubernetes/manifests` and are managed by the kubelet, not the API server. Editing the manifest and letting the kubelet restart the Pod recovers the scheduler without a cluster reset.

title: Repair CoreDNS and configure Pod DNS
instructions: The CoreDNS Corefile forwards external lookups to an unreachable resolver (`1.2.3.4`). Repair the `coredns` ConfigMap in `kube-system` to forward through `/etc/resolv.conf`, reload CoreDNS, then create a Pod named `dns-app` in `exam-repair` with `dnsConfig` nameservers `1.1.1.1` and search domain `example.test`.
steps: Inspect with `kubectl -n kube-system get cm coredns -o yaml` and locate the broken `forward . 1.2.3.4` line.
Edit the ConfigMap to use `forward . /etc/resolv.conf`.
Reload with `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns`.
Create the Pod `dns-app` with the required `dnsConfig` (nameservers and searches).
solution:
kubectl -n kube-system get cm coredns -o json | jq '.data.Corefile = (.data.Corefile | split("forward . 1.2.3.4") | join("forward . /etc/resolv.conf"))' | kubectl apply -f -
kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
kubectl apply -f - <<'YAML'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: dns-app
  namespace: exam-repair
spec:
  containers:
    - name: app
      image: busybox:1.36
      command: ["sh", "-c", "sleep 3600"]
  dnsConfig:
    nameservers:
      - 1.1.1.1
    searches:
      - example.test
YAML
resource: jq -n --argjson cm "$(kubectl -n kube-system get cm coredns -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson pod "$(kubectl -n exam-repair get pod dns-app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{configmap:$cm,pod:$pod}'

checks.expression: (.configmap != null) and ((.configmap.data.Corefile // "") | contains("forward . /etc/resolv.conf")) and (((.configmap.data.Corefile // "") | contains("1.2.3.4")) | not)

checks.description: Application Pod has custom DNS settings

explanation: CoreDNS resolves cluster names and forwards the rest. A bad `forward` line breaks external resolution until the Corefile is corrected and CoreDNS reloaded. A Pod's `dnsConfig` overrides nameservers and search domains for that Pod.

title: Repair a Service selector and targetPort
instructions: The Service `backend-svc` in `exam-repair` has no endpoints because its selector and targetPort are wrong. The backing Pods are labeled `app=backend` and listen on port 8080. Repair the Service so it has at least one ready endpoint.
steps: Compare `kubectl -n exam-repair get svc backend-svc -o yaml` with `kubectl -n exam-repair get pods --show-labels`.
Fix the selector to `app: backend`.
Fix the port's `targetPort` to 8080 (the container port).
Verify with `kubectl -n exam-repair get endpointslices -l kubernetes.io/service-name=backend-svc`.
solution: kubectl -n exam-repair patch service backend-svc --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/selector","value":{"app":"backend"}},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/ports/0/targetPort","value":8080}]'
resource: jq -n --argjson svc "$(kubectl -n exam-repair get svc backend-svc -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson eps "$(kubectl -n exam-repair get endpointslice -l kubernetes.io/service-name=backend-svc -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" '{service:$svc,endpoints:$eps}'

checks.expression: (.endpoints != null) and any(.endpoints.items[]?; any(.endpoints[]?; (.conditions.ready != false) and (.addresses | length) > 0))

explanation: Endpoints are derived from the Service selector; a mismatch leaves the Service without backends. `targetPort` must name the port the container actually listens on, or traffic is dropped.

title: Diagnose and fix an OOM-killed workload
instructions: The Deployment `oom-app` in `exam-repair` is OOM-killed because its memory limit (50Mi) is below its allocation. Use `kubectl describe` and `kubectl get events` to diagnose it, raise the memory limit to at least 128Mi, save your evidence to `/tmp/oom-evidence.txt`, and confirm the Pod becomes available.
steps: Diagnose with `kubectl -n exam-repair describe pod -l app=oom-app` and `kubectl -n exam-repair get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp`.
Save the evidence with `kubectl -n exam-repair describe pod -l app=oom-app > /tmp/oom-evidence.txt`.
Raise the container memory limit to at least 128Mi with `kubectl -n exam-repair edit deployment oom-app`.
Wait with `kubectl -n exam-repair rollout status deployment/oom-app`.
solution:
kubectl -n exam-repair describe pod -l app=oom-app > /tmp/oom-evidence.txt
kubectl -n exam-repair patch deployment oom-app --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/memory","value":"256Mi"}]'
kubectl -n exam-repair rollout status deployment/oom-app --timeout=180s
resource: jq -n --argjson dep "$(kubectl -n exam-repair get deployment oom-app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson evidence "$(test -s /tmp/oom-evidence.txt && echo true || echo false)" '{deployment:$dep,evidence:$evidence}'
explanation: A container that exceeds its memory limit is OOM-killed and restarted in a loop. `kubectl describe` and events surface the kill; raising the limit and saving the diagnostic output documents the fix.

title: Recover a multi-container crash
instructions: Both containers in the Deployment `crash-app` in `exam-repair` exit immediately. Use current and previous logs (`kubectl logs -p`) to diagnose, save the previous logs to `/tmp/crash-logs.txt`, repair the container commands so they keep running, and confirm the Pod is available.
steps: Diagnose with `kubectl -n exam-repair logs -l app=crash-app --all-containers --previous`.
Save evidence with `kubectl -n exam-repair logs -l app=crash-app --all-containers --previous > /tmp/crash-logs.txt`.
Patch both container commands to `["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]`.
Wait with `kubectl -n exam-repair rollout status deployment/crash-app`.
solution:
kubectl -n exam-repair logs -l app=crash-app --all-containers --previous > /tmp/crash-logs.txt 2>/dev/null || true
kubectl -n exam-repair patch deployment crash-app --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/command","value":["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]},{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/1/command","value":["sh","-c","sleep 3600"]}]'
kubectl -n exam-repair rollout status deployment/crash-app --timeout=180s
resource: jq -n --argjson dep "$(kubectl -n exam-repair get deployment crash-app -o json 2>/dev/null || echo null)" --argjson evidence "$(test -s /tmp/crash-logs.txt && echo true || echo false)" '{deployment:$dep,evidence:$evidence}'

checks.expression: (.deployment != null) and ([.deployment.spec.template.spec.containers[] | ((.command // []) | map(tostring) | join(" "))] | map(select(contains("exit 1"))) | length) == 0

explanation: `kubectl logs --previous` shows the output of a container's prior (crashed) invocation. Replacing the immediate-exit command with a long-running one stops the CrashLoopBackOff and restores availability.
